full_judgment:
In the instant Civil Revision, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 19-6-2000 and 26-9-2000 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Mymensingh in Family Appeal No. 35 of 1998 reserving the judgment and decree dated 18-5-1998 and 27-5-1998 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Haluaghat, Mymensingh, in Family Suit No. 06 of 1996 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 6. The trial Court on consideration of the material evidence on record decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 18-5-1998 for an amount of Taka 43,250 (forty three thousand two hundred fifty) and Taka 500 (five hundred) per month. And against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court the defendant preferred appeal being Family Appeal No. 35 of 1998 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh, who transferred the same to the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Mymensingh for disposal. The learned Additional District Judge heard the appeal and without considering the material evidence on record and allowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 19-9-2000 and dismissed the suit. 

 19. On perusal of the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the petition, the impugned judgment, as well as, the judgment of the trial Court and the LCR it is quite evident to note that there is hardly any dispute with regard to the facts except that the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff, wherein it is clearly described that the opposite party husband used to physically and mentally torture the petitioner, which the learned judge of the appellate Court did not controvert, however, he without any substantial basis reversed this finding. 

 (7) for any other justifiable cause: Provided that a Hindu married woman shall not be entitled to separate residence and maintenance from her husband if she is unchaste or ceases to be a Hindu by change to another religion or fails without sufficient cause to comply with a decree of a competent Court for the restitution of conjugal rights. 

 26. In the result, the Rule is made Absolute. The judgment and decree dated 19-6-2000 and 26-9-2000 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Mymensingh in Family Appeal No. 35 of 1998 is hereby set aside; and the judgment and decree dated 18-5-1998 and 27-5-1998 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Haluaghat, Mymensingh, in Family Suit No. 06 of 1996 are hereby maintained.
